messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 57 omitted, sha256 11587dd1a24ef8fd>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 60
reason: Clause 3.2 lets the receiving party make electronic copies reasonably inaccessible instead of deleting them, which means those copies are still retained after return or destruction.
<quote check="exact">or make them reasonably inaccessible</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 80
reason: Clause 3.2 expressly states that PwC, as a receiving party, may not retain a copy of the confidential information after return or destruction, which contradicts the hypothesis.
<quote check="exact">However, PwC may not retain a copy of the confidential information for our internal purposes.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 70
reason: The agreement requires destroying or returning all confidential information and expressly says PwC may not retain a copy, though the option to make electronic copies 'reasonably inaccessible' leaves some ambiguity.
<quote check="exact">either destroy or return all confidential information to the disclosing party</quote>
<quote check="exact">However, PwC may not retain a copy of the confidential information for our internal purposes.</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Entailment", "confidence": 60, "quotes": ["in the case of electronic copies of confidential information, delete them or make them reasonably inaccessible"], "reason": "Clause 3.2 lets the receiving party make electronic copies reasonably inaccessible instead of deleting them, so some confidential information can stay in its possession after return or destruction, even though PwC specifically may not keep a copy for internal purposes."}
